blocks.h2: Why Flushing Matters With Evanston Water
blocks.body: Evanston's water is hard, around 7.8 grains per gallon. As water heats, some of those minerals settle to the bottom of the tank as sediment. Over time, that layer insulates the water from the burner, so the heater works harder, makes popping sounds and wears out sooner. A yearly flush drains the sediment before it hardens. If your heater has never been flushed, we'll tell you whether it's still worth doing.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Questions From Evanston Homeowners

items.q: Is it worth repairing an older heater?
items.preview: Under 8 years, usually. Over 12, usually not.
items.answer: Under about 8 years, a repair usually makes sense. Past 12, or with a leaking tank, replacement is the better value.

items.q: Why does my heater make popping noises?
items.preview: Sediment on the bottom of the tank.
items.answer: Sediment is trapping water under it, and the bubbles pop as it heats. A flush can help if it's caught early.

items.q: Does Evanston's water shorten heater life?
items.answer: At about 7.8 grains per gallon, sediment builds up over time. Flushing once a year helps.

items.q: How long do water heaters last?
Can I flush my water heater myself?
items.answer: You can, with a hose on the drain valve. Be careful with hot water and an old valve that may not close again.
